::: {#rem-score-surprisal}
#### The score is the negative derivative of the surprisal

For a [continuous](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-continuous-rv) $\vX$ with
[density](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pdf) $\p(\vx \mid \param)$,
the [surprisal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/entropy.html#def-surprisal)
of the data value $\vx$ under parameter value $\param$ is $-\log \p(\vx \mid \param)$,
which is minus the [log-likelihood](#def-loglik) $-\llik(\param)$.
So the [score](#def-score) is minus the derivative of the surprisal with respect to $\param$.
By @thm-information-equality,
the [expected information](#def-einf) is the expected squared derivative of the surprisal,
with the [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) taken over the data $\vX$ when the parameter is $\param$:
$\einf(\param) = \E{\score^2}$.
:::
